# Danske Regioner

Danske Regioner (Danish Regions) is the organization referenced in the ADHD-database's 2024 annual report as the body — alongside the Danish Health Authority (Sundhedsstyrelsen) — that has reviewed and signed off on which health professionals are qualified to issue psychiatric diagnoses [^src1]. Specifically, the report states that Danske Regioner has approved the practice of allowing Specialpsykologer (specialist psychologists) to be included in diagnostic criteria used within the national ADHD-database, and that neither Danske Regioner nor Sundhedsstyrelsen has raised any objection ("forbehold") to this arrangement [^src1][^src2].

This matters because the ADHD-database is a nationwide registry covering children, adolescents, and adults with ADHD, built around two population tracks — an assessment ("udredning") population and a treatment population [^src1]. As part of the report's appendix documenting calculation rules and regional feedback, several of Denmark's five regions flagged registration and implementation problems with specific indicators [^src1]. Region Sjælland in particular pushed for Specialpsykologer to be formally counted toward the diagnostic criterion for indicator 3, citing their legally established authority to make psychiatric diagnoses [^src1]. Danske Regioner's endorsement — together with that of Sundhedsstyrelsen — is cited as the basis on which this inclusion was accepted without reservation, confirming that specialist psychologists' diagnostic competence is recognized at the national administrative level [^src1][^src2].

No further relationships, claims, or timeline events involving Danske Regioner appear in the available corpus.
